title: Overnight handoff: contradictions & probation sketch
content:
Notes to self (overnight handoff) — candidate: Damien Ortiz
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference) — final onsite loop, 2026-03-10
Purpose: capture contradictions across interviews, potential probation plan if hired, and open verification questions for next-day sync with hiring committee.

High-level impression
- Very strong systems intuition for memory and KV-cache tradeoffs. Good mental model for shader/kernel selection tradeoffs at a high level, but vague on specific profiling methodology used at scale.
- Personality: calm, pragmatic; good on cross-team tradeoffs. Might under-communicate risk impact (tends to downplay complexity).

Contradictions observed (by interviewer) — record each, why it matters
1) Quantization experience
   - Interviewer A: said they shipped 8-bit INT quantization pipelines in prod using bitsandbytes + custom kernels, named specific tuning heuristics (layer-wise calibration).
   - Interviewer B: candidate said "I prototyped a quantized pipeline but I didnt own productionization; infra team did the final rollout."
   - Why it matters: ownership level mismatch — if they claim autonomous quantization ops but actually havent surfaced infra edge cases (OOM, perf regressions), they may overpromise on ramp speed for Optimize work.

2) Load testing and profiling
   - Interviewer C: candidate discussed microbenchmarking on A100 and p4d, produced latency tail charts in description.
   - Interviewer D: when pressed for metrics, candidate deferred to "I dont have the exact numbers here" and could not sketch distribution assumptions.
   - Why it matters: good at concept-level testing but may lack reproducible benchmark artifacts. For Dedicated capacity commitments, we need engineers who can produce reproducible workflows.

3) Leadership vs IC growth signals
   - Candidate describes mentoring and code review cadence, has led small migrations. But when asked about roadmap tradeoffs and prioritization, reverted to "do the safe thing" instead of advocating product-level tradeoffs.
   - Why: could be excellent IC contributor but unclear readiness to balance product vs infra when negotiating SLA tradeoffs with product managers.

Quick score (subjective, 1-5)
- Systems/infra depth: 4
- Production ownership: 3
- Scaling/bench expertise: 3
- Collaboration/communication: 4
- Ramp to senior: 3

Top strengths
- Clear mental model for KV cache and prefix caching strategies; sketches of cache invalidation flows were crisp.
- Pragmatic debugging approach: triage-first, isolate kernel vs orchestration.
- Comfortable reading and reasoning about low-level CUDA/MLPerf-ish constraints though not a kernel author.

Top risks / red flags
- Ambiguity in concrete ownership of quantization and load-testing artifacts (see contradictions).
- Slight tendency to understate potential downstream costs (e.g., not surfacing how cache warming affects tail latency).
- Limited experience negotiating SLA tradeoffs with PMs at scale (could slow decisions on rollouts).

Suggested verification questions for follow-up (small async checks before committing)
- Ask for two PRs or diffs where they were the primary author for a production quantization/precision change (links + short explanation). Verify they handled rollback/fallback and post-mortem.
- Request a short reproducible benchmark (script + expected output) that reproduces a claimed latency improvement. Even a toy harness is fine.
- Ask for a one-paragraph summary of a prioritization decision they made where they pushed back on product and explain the tradeoffs and outcome.

If hired: proposed 90-day probation blueprint (aimed at addressable gaps)
- Week 1-2: onboarding + small infra read-only tasks, pair with SRE on test infra.
- Week 3-6: own a small perf/latency story — e.g., end-to-end profiling on a model in staging and deliver a reproducible benchmark + comparison (goal: show ownership of profiling artifacts).
- Week 7-12: lead a rollbackable experiment — implement a quantization pilot on a non-critical workload, create rollout plan, fallbacks, and a short post-mortem. This tests both quantization claims and rollout discipline.
- Checkpoints: 30/60/90 with engineering manager and two cross-functional stakeholders (SRE, product).

Hiring-readiness recommendation (quick)
- Hire with conditions: yes, contingent on 1) evidence of primary ownership of at least one production quantization change or 2) a reproducible benchmark artifact within 2 weeks of offer acceptance.
- Rationale: candidate has high upside for runtime optimization role but we need to mitigate ambiguous ownership signals.

Notes for debrief meeting (bullet points to be spoken)
- "Damien shows strong infra intuition; primary concern is concrete ownership evidence for quantization and reproducible profiling."
- "Recommend conditional hire — require small deliverables post-offer rather than re-open loop."
- "If we dont get the artifacts, consider extending probation with specific measurable goals."

Open questions / unresolved items
- Did they ever author a rollback plan that was executed? Which incident? (I flagged this to Juno).
- Whats the precise cadence they ran for load tests at previous employer (frequency, CI hooks)?
- Does the candidate have experience with multi-tenant isolation policies in GPU pools? Interviewers described different answers.

Slack/PR references to attach to offer (if any)
- Link: ask candidate for 2 PR links + a 2-3 paragraph companion note explaining their role in each. Put those in the offer packet and mark as condition.

Mini action items (next 24 hours)
- Send candidate chase-email template with two asks (PR links, toy benchmark) — draft below. Owner: Amina.
- Add conditional-offer language to HR draft (Juno + Marcus to review).
- Schedule 30-minute async debrief with interviewers to reconcile the contradictory threads (Marcus to run).

Draft email to candidate (quick sketch)
Hi Damien — enjoyed meeting you yesterday. As a next step for our final checks, could you share 1) links to up to two PRs where you were primary author for a production change related to quantization or inference performance, and 2) a short reproducible benchmark script (or a one-paragraph description of the steps + expected numbers) that demonstrates a latency or memory improvement you helped deliver? If you dont have exact artifacts, a short writeup of the change and what you owned will work.
Thanks — Amina

Personal scratch/thoughts (unpolished)
- If candidate is truthful, very valuable for Optimize team later. If candidate exaggerating, still solid IC for runtime but less for lead infra projects.
- Tension: we need someone who can ship bench+rollout artifacts quickly. Conditioned offer seems low-friction and high-signal.
- Could pair them on an initial GD/Experiment with someone senior from SRE to accelerate verification.

End of notes.
